chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Get the best shrouds for your dead ones, for these are their adornments.

key_terms.أَكْفَان: Shrouds (plural of كَفَن, kafan) used to wrap the body for burial.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for choosing shrouds for the deceased in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the virtue of hastening to provide superior shrouds, framing this act as a form of honor and adornment for the deceased in their transition to the grave. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on dignified burial practices as an extension of respect for the human body, which is considered a trust from God. The instruction to 'hasten' (ajidū) also reflects the broader Islamic principle of promptness in funeral rites, linking physical care of the body with spiritual reverence.
